question: How much will Nvidia's stock price returns exceed Microsoft's in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: rolling ~9-10-trading-day NVDA-minus-MSFT price-return spreads through 2025-26, whose 2026 mean runs about +1.5pp per window (NVDA up modestly-to-+20% YTD vs MSFT roughly -20%) with very large dispersion. I anchor the center well below that drift: two-week cross-sectional momentum has near-zero predictive power, NVDA has run +10.2% in 7 sessions into its 52-week high of 236.54 (short-term reversal risk), MSFT is deeply de-rated with its own building catalysts (first standalone Azure revenue disclosure, 42% growth, backlog, analyst target hikes), and NVDA goes ex-dividend Sep 10 (-0.11pp on price return). The dominant feature is width, not direction: I computed the spread SD directly from Aug 4-Sep 4 closes at 2.75%/day ex-earnings, driven by a striking -0.29 realized correlation (AI-hardware/AI-software rotation); blending that noisy correlation toward +0.1 still leaves ~7 pp of SD over 9 sessions. A live coin-flip FOMC hike decision on Sep 16 (Kalshi ~48%, futures 56-66%) sits inside the window and cuts both ways with more force on the higher-beta leg. Escape mass is real but small: NVDA alone moved +8.7% in one session on Aug 27 while MSFT moved +1.8%, and DeepSeek-type AI-capex shocks have produced >15pp single-day spreads before; I price 2.5% above +15 (China Blackwell/H200 export opening or an AI melt-up plus an MSFT capex/yield de-rating) and 2.0% below -15 (AI-capex scare, hawkish Fed hit to high-multiple hardware, memory/gross-margin shock). Evidence is genuinely two-sided and I stay close to the reference class.

calls.reasoning: Nine sessions (Sep 7 is Labor Day), no earnings for either name - NVDA reported Aug 26, MSFT reports Oct 27 - which strips out the driver that dominates the raw sample (MSFT's +15.5% Jul 30 gap produced 10-day spreads of -18 to -26pp). The clean reference class centers near zero with SD ~5pp. I set the median at +0.2: the beta differential (2.22 vs 1.11) against positive drift is worth ~+0.3pp, offset by NVDA's -0.11pp Sep 10 ex-div and short-horizon reversal after +7.5% in ten sessions into a 52-week high. I do not carry Run 1's 2026 NVDA-drift adjustment - the YTD figures behind it are contradictory across vendors and two-week cross-sectional momentum has no predictive power. Width is the real question and I land at 5.7pp SD, below Run 1's 7pp (its -0.29 correlation is a 23-session artifact contradicted by two 40-session samples AND by the option-implied cross-check) but above the naive ex-earnings 5.2pp, because the correlation parameter is genuinely unpinned and a live FOMC, quad-witching, and an NVDA-only conference slot all sit inside the window. No human market prices this spread: checked Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold - Kalshi/Polymarket Nvidia contracts are GPU rental prices, and the harness-supplied Manifold market (Big Tech vs Bitcoin, 0.84, ~$2.9k volume, closes 2030) matches on no term that matters, so no blend.
calls.reconciliation: Six factual disputes and one judgment call. (1) The decisive one was daily NVDA-MSFT correlation: Run 1's -0.29 over 23 sessions implied a 7pp spread SD and a 17-point width; Runs 2 and 3 independently got +0.45-0.6 over 40 sessions implying 5.0-5.3pp. I settled it against Run 1 - larger sample, two independent agreeing computations, Run 1's own admission that its sample is noisy and that the historical correlation is positive, and an independent option-implied check (32.7%/23.9% IVs) that reproduces 5.0-5.5pp and not 7pp. But because the estimate genuinely spans -0.29 to +0.6, I priced the parameter uncertainty rather than collapsing to 5.2, landing at 5.7pp SD / 14.6 width - inside Runs 2 and 3, well below Run 1. (2) NVDA's Sep 10 $0.25 ex-dividend: Runs 1 and 3 give the same date and amount, Run 2 denies it citing a yield figure that looks stale; two-to-one, accepted, worth -0.11pp. (3) Run 3 found NVDA presenting at Goldman Communacopia Sep 10 while Runs 1 and 2 searched and found nothing - a specific positive finding beats failed searches, so I count it as an NVDA-only headline vector that widens without directing. (4) MSFT 30d IV of 23.9% accepted from Run 3 as the only retrieved value and consistent with beta 1.11 and no earnings. (5) FOMC hike odds (Kalshi 48% vs FedWatch 68%) could NOT be settled from the dossiers - different venues, different dates - and I let it stand as two-sided variance on the higher-beta leg, not a direction. (6) 2026 YTD relative performance is irreconcilable across vendor snippets and I declined to build any drift on it. (7) The median sign is pure judgment with no evidence breaking the tie; I take the bet Runs 1 and 2 take (positive) at roughly half their magnitude, since the reversal and ex-div arguments Run 3 raises are real but small. I carried Run 2's reference class forward - it is the right conditioning set, since whether the window contains earnings is KNOWN here, not uncertain. No sources retrieved on this run.

disagreements.verdict: Settled toward positive: 40-session sample beats 23-session, two runs agree independently, Run 1 concedes its sample is noisy and the historical correlation positive, and the option-implied cross-check (NVDA IV 32.7%, MSFT 23.9%) reproduces 5.0-5.5pp. Residual spread in the estimate priced as extra width: SD 5.7, not 5.2 and not 7.

disagreements.verdict: Resolved in favor of Runs 1 and 3 - same date and same amount from two independent runs; Run 2's 0.005% yield reads as a stale pre-raise figure. Effect is -0.11pp on the spread, immaterial to the percentiles.

disagreements.verdict: Accepted as the only retrieved value; consistent with MSFT beta 1.11 and no earnings in the window. Used in the implied-vol dispersion cross-check.

disagreements.verdict: COULD NOT BE SETTLED from the dossiers - different venues sampled on different dates. Carried as genuine uncertainty: the meeting is a live two-sided event that raises dispersion on the higher-beta leg, with no directional read either way.

disagreements.claim: NVDA has a positive 2026 drift versus MSFT worth ~+1.5pp per two-week window (Run 1)
disagreements.verdict: COULD NOT BE SETTLED - the underlying YTD figures span NVDA +4% to +21% and MSFT -20% to +3% across vendors, and both other dossiers flag them as irreconcilable. Discounted entirely; two-week cross-sectional momentum has near-zero predictive power regardless.

disagreements.claim: Median spread is slightly positive (+0.4/+0.5, Runs 1-2) vs slightly negative (-0.3, Run 3)
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks this tie. The beta differential against positive drift (~+0.3pp) is a real mechanism; the ex-div drag (-0.11pp) and reversal after +7.5% into a 52-week high are also real but smaller. I take the positive side at half the magnitude: +0.2.
